analysis.title: Global Credit Trader: AI-Related Supply: Outlining the Directional Risks
key_insights: Hyperscaler year-to-date global debt issuance has reached $296 billion, above GS's full-year 2026 forecast of $250 billion. Five bond deals totaling $67 billion have priced since October 29.

YTD hyperscaler issuance equals 36% of GIR equity research's 2026 Capex forecast, above GS's initial expectation of 33% debt funded. Some of this is a pull-forward of planned 2027 supply, per company commentary.
GS sees scope for more front-loading of issuance, highly dependent on market tone. Between now and early December, risks to its spread forecasts are firmly tilted toward more widening.
GS still assumes 35% of hyperscaler Capex is debt financed in 2027, about $440 billion of direct issuance, plus an additional $300 billion of project finance issuance across IG and HY.
The HY primary market may be in a price discovery phase in the near term, with a sharp focus on structures for project finance deals once issuance resumes.
Delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments are the key risks to more debt issuance. Faster near-term monetization of AI investment is the key risk to less debt issuance.
Hyperscalers collectively reported negative free cash flow in 3Q2026 because capital expenditure outpaced operating cash flow, which increased the role of debt financing.

GS has tracked more than $687 billion of global AI-related debt issuance YTD across syndicated IG, HY and leveraged loans. Only 43% was issued directly by the five hyperscalers. $568 billion is in IG and $119 billion in leveraged finance.
AI-related issuance in the EUR IG market has accelerated, but its share of total gross supply remains below USD, GBP and CAD. GS sees room for EUR AI-related issuance to grow.

USD IG has had 27 jumbo deals of $10 billion or more YTD, totaling $501 billion. 14 of them, and 66% of jumbo deal value, were AI-related. AI-related deals price with larger new issue concessions than non-AI deals.

GS economists expect short-term data center moratoriums from Democratic wins at the state and local level, potentially affecting about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion. Texas is 25% of planned capacity. They expect moratoriums to be short-lived and the midterms to change little for federal data center and AI regulation.

GS keeps a bottom-up, selective approach to project finance deals. Offtaker quality, principal coverage and refinancing economics matter, and macro-driven widening should offer entry points for well-underwritten deals.
Meta's SEC filing said timing is important to secure capital before competitors saturate funding options for the same AI growth.
GS expects the AI issuance cycle to use private markets as well, which can offer certainty of execution on large bespoke financings.
GS no longer sees an outright IG overweight vs HY as clear in either USD or EUR, based on valuations, rate sensitivity and supply technicals. Its view is neutral IG vs HY.

GS expects BBs to face a challenging supply technical from AI-related supply and favors Bs in USD. It prefers HY bonds over loans because of loan market software exposure and the 2028 maturity wall, and prefers CLO mezzanine tranches over leveraged loans.
GS has a slight preference for USD credit over EUR, and overweights BBBs vs higher-rated cohorts in both markets. It prefers Agency MBS vs IG corporates.

sector_views.rationale: Neutral IG vs HY on valuations, rate sensitivity and AI-related supply technicals. Overweight BBBs vs As and AAs to capture spread.
Overweight Bs, neutral BBs, underweight CCCs. BBs face a challenging supply technical from AI-related issuance.
Overweight HY bonds vs loans because of heavy software exposure, the 2028 maturity wall, lower-rated distribution and limited carry pickup.
Neutral IG vs HY. Favors BBBs over AAs and As given an improved macro backdrop supporting a down-in-quality stance.
Overweight CLO mezzanine tranches vs leveraged loans on low historical impairment and attractive carry. Neutral senior CLO vs USD IG, would add on spread widening.

earnings_insights: Hyperscalers (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle) collectively reported negative free cash flow in 3Q2026 as capex outpaced cash flow from operations, per GS equity portfolio strategy.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Year-end tightening is forecast on seasonal slowing of supply, but risks to the forecast are tilted toward widening before early December. GS expects a modest overshoot of the March 2026 peak of 93bp.
Forecast reflects modestly tighter levels than today. The March 2026 peak was 335bp.
April 2025 levels are viewed as appropriate for a near-term downside scenario.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight USD credit vs EUR credit
trade_ideas.rationale: A somewhat more challenging growth-inflation-monetary policy mix in the Euro Area.
trade_ideas.risk: Lines are blurring between regional classifications as cross-border issuance accelerates.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight BBBs vs higher-rated (A and AA) USD IG cohorts
trade_ideas.rationale: Captures additional spread and GS sees scope for balance sheet deterioration at the highest end of the rating spectrum.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight B-rated USD HY, neutral BBs, underweight CCCs
trade_ideas.rationale: BBs face a challenging supply technical from AI-related supply. CCC is highly idiosyncratic.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight HY bonds vs leveraged loans
trade_ideas.rationale: Substantial software exposure in the loan market until clarity on refinancing of the 2028 maturity wall, lower-rated distribution of loans, and limited carry pickup vs HY.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight CLO mezzanine tranches vs leveraged loans
trade_ideas.rationale: Low historical impairment rates for BB and BBB CLO tranches, attractive carry and a cushion against moderate to elevated default outcomes.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight EUR IG CLO tranches vs USD IG CLO tranches
trade_ideas.rationale: Carry pickup, and subordination protects tranches higher in the capital structure from idiosyncratic defaults.
trade_ideas.risk: Less supportive policy and macro picture in Europe.

trade_ideas.rationale: Additional spread compensation viewed as moderately attractive, with the hybrid premium expected to compress as the market grows.

trade_ideas.description: Prefer Agency MBS vs IG corporate bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: Diversification benefit vs a portfolio of IG corporate bonds.

risk_factors: Delayed monetization of AI investment and growth in purchase commitments could drive more debt issuance and wider spreads.
Spread risk through early December is tilted toward more widening, with a modest overshoot of the March 2026 USD peaks (93bp IG, 335bp HY) expected.
Short-term data center moratoriums could affect about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion.
HY primary market in price discovery phase, with focus on project finance structures.
Offtaker quality, principal coverage and refinancing economics are key risks for project finance deals.
Software sector exposure in the loan market and the 2028 loan maturity wall.
Negative hyperscaler free cash flow in 3Q2026 increases dependence on debt markets and exposes issuers to market tone.
Concentrated AI-related primary issuance, with larger new issue concessions than non-AI deals.

GS expects increased investor selectivity on where and at what price to take AI-related credit exposure as allocators balance exposure across equities, syndicated credit and private markets.

tension_points.bull_case: Acceleration in near-term monetization of AI investment would mean less debt issuance and relieve spread pressure.
tension_points.bear_case: Delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments, which are additional uses of cash separate from Capex, would drive more debt issuance and wider spreads.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Faster near-term monetization of AI investment would invalidate the case for more issuance.

tension_points.bull_case: Typical late-December spread tightening as supply slows supports GS's year-end targets, which are modestly tighter than current levels (USD IG 82bp, HY 295bp).
tension_points.bear_case: Between now and early December, front-loaded and pull-forward AI issuance could produce a more volatile backdrop and a modest overshoot of the March 2026 peaks (93bp IG, 335bp HY).
tension_points.what_invalidates: USD IG spreads moving above the March 2026 peak of 93bp, or HY above 335bp, before the seasonal slowdown in supply.
